title: The blame walk reads a cancelled main run as unknown, never as a skip, and names a re-run first
why: A commit whose main run was cancelled has no verdict, so the walk can blame the wrong merge.
source: Lane merge-flow-after-anthropic (session_013NEJL2oxYMVKoXseeKacVG), R42 part 2 fix-after, via the coordinator 15:36 CST Nov 13; read at main 59da758a3. Item (d).
note: Filed 15:36 CST Nov 13. File and symbol: merge/merge.py base_state and breaking_line, the walk over main's push runs of `checks` (about L1543-1550 per retro; the lane did not re-read it). It steps over cancelled runs. Main's six R42 merge commits (1476f3491, 7ff000630, f1b8031f1, e11e5ef04, 15431d2ec, 59da758a3) had four cancelled runs, one gone, one running at 15:34 CST (an audit agent's read). Fix: a cancelled run reads as unknown; the walk names a re-run (gh run rerun) before any blame. Test: a cancelled run between a green and a red run, red on main. A check change: test-author red case first, builder, reviewer. Overlaps: blame-on-finished-red-job, runner-blame-one-merge, lint-clash-blames-wrong-pr (check before a lane starts). Past rulings not checked; measures are the lane's and retro's, unread by triage.
